speaker: Doctor
text: I see the previous note suggests a diagnosis, but I need to evaluate your specific symptoms of shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To begin, can you tell me exactly how long it has been since your surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned pain when eating and difficulty wearing earrings; do you also experience a feeling of pressure or fullness in your right ear, and have you noticed any drainage or changes in hearing since your tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy. REQUEST IMAGES: Post-op Ear_Images.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy shows clear tympanic membranes bilaterally with no evidence of active drainage, perforation, or granulation tissue. The right ear demonstrates intact surgical grafts consistent with the tympanoplasty performed 12 weeks ago. Post-op Ear_Images confirm proper graft placement and healing of the right middle ear cavity with no signs of recurrent infection or fluid accumulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The otoscopy and images confirm your graft is healing well with no active infection or drainage. Since the mechanical structure is intact but you feel shooting pain when eating and discomfort with earrings, could you describe exactly where the pain is located on the pinna or in the ear canal, and does it trigger a facial twitch or sensation when you chew?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Great Auricular Nerve Entrapment / Neuralgia. The combination of shooting pain triggered by eating and specific discomfort with earrings (which press on the mastoid/tail of the ear where the nerve is harvested) in the context of a recent tympanoplasty is highly characteristic of entrapment or irritation of the Great Auricular Nerve. The positive response to pressure (earrings) and the nature of the pain (shooting) rule out common middle ear pathologies given the normal otoscopy.
